whatItIs.text: The juice of pressed olives — one of the three core food plants of Mediterranean cuisine alongside wheat and grapes; extra-virgin grade must have no more than 0.8% free acidity.

historyNote.text: Olives have been cultivated around the Mediterranean since the 8th millennium BC, and wild ones were gathered even earlier; Greece spread the cosmetic-and-athlete oil habit through its gymnasia, where oil stayed in use for nearly a thousand years.

howToChoose.text: Buy dark bottles with a harvest date (not just a best-before) — fresher is sharper and grassier; for cooking choose a modest everyday oil and save the peppery extra-virgin for finishing.

storage.text: Keep cool and away from light in a dark bottle; oil does not improve with age.

foodSafetyRef.note: Practice storage guidance only; no rulebook content is claimed. The app's food-safety rules live in data/food-safety/rules.json.

useItUp.text: Aging oil still fries and bakes; whisk it into dressings, drizzle over soup, or freeze in ice-cube trays with herbs for instant flavour bombs.

substitutions.note: neutral for high-heat cooking; no fruitiness
for baking where dairy flavour helps
